numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For a Timestamp near the int64 upper bound (e.g. pd.Timestamp("2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807")), tz_localize to a DST zone reports an ordinary wall time as a nonexistent time (ValueError) or silently returns NaT with nonexistent="NaT"; in fixed-offset or machine-local timezones, two or more values near Timestamp.min/max came back wrapped into the year -2262 because the shift used a bare subtraction that wrapped int64.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The out-of-range UTC conversion should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime (e.g. "Converting ... overflows past 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807"), not a nonexistent-time ValueError, not NaT, and not a wrapped int64 value; a shift landing exactly on the NaT sentinel should also raise OutOfBoundsDatetime rather than be returned as missing data.
trigger_conditions: Timestamp value near the int64 upper bound (around 2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807) localized with tz_localize to America/New_York
Same wall time in a zone with no DST rule such as America/Panama
tz_localize with nonexistent="NaT" on such a value
Two or more values near Timestamp.min/max in a fixed-offset or machine-local timezone (use_tzlocal/use_fixed loops)
A shift that lands exactly on the NaT sentinel value

input_output_examples.buggy_output: ValueError: ... is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time

oracle_clues: Fix described as making unrepresentable results raise OutOfBoundsDatetime instead of wrapping int64 or returning the NaT sentinel
Regression test reproducer given in PR#66698 with before/after behaviour
Related issue references GH#65733 and GH#66550

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Values near Timestamp.min/max (int64 bounds, e.g. Timestamp.max._value - 2*3600*10**9 and -(2**63) + 9*3600*10**9); example Timestamp 2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807 localized to America/New_York
category_specific_evidence: Correctness property violated: a local->UTC shift must not wrap int64; a UTC result outside representable range must raise OutOfBoundsDatetime rather than wrap or return NaT sentinel
Wrap example: two or more values near Timestamp.max in a fixed-offset timezone wrapped to year -2262 instead of raising (bare subtraction in use_fixed/use_tzlocal loops)

Reproducer: ts = pd.Timestamp('2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807'); ts.tz_localize('America/New_York') previously raised misleading ValueError about nonexistent time; now OutOfBoundsDatetime 'overflows past 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807'
ts.tz_localize('America/New_York', nonexistent='NaT') previously returned NaT silently; now OutOfBoundsDatetime

Sentinel case: shift landing exactly on NaT sentinel (-(2**63) + 9*3600*10**9 as M8[ns]) is one below minimum representable value and must raise OutOfBoundsDatetime with 'underflows past' instead of being stored as missing data
Length-1 DatetimeIndex masks the bug because the lone value is boxed downstream; reproduction needs >= 2 values for fixed-offset case

Past-last-cached-transition case: DatetimeIndex([Timestamp(Timestamp.max._value - 2*3600*10**9)]).tz_localize('America/New_York') with kwargs {} / nonexistent='NaT' / nonexistent='shift_forward' must raise OutOfBoundsDatetime 'overflows past'
Related issues GH#65733 and GH#66550; PR#66698
reproduction_risks: Length-1 DatetimeIndex inputs may not expose the fixed-offset overflow because boxing catches it downstream
Machine-local timezone (use_tzlocal) behavior depends on the local system timezone, which the passages do not specify
Exact expected error message text is only partially given ('underflows past', 'overflows past') and should be matched loosely

provenance.value: For a Timestamp near the int64 upper bound (e.g. pd.Timestamp("2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807")), tz_localize to a DST zone reports an ordinary wall time as a nonexistent time (ValueError) or silently returns NaT with nonexistent="NaT"; in fixed-offset or machine-local timezones, two or more values near Timestamp.min/max came back wrapped into the year -2262 because the shift used a bare subtraction that wrapped int64.
